property_summary: After a successful go call with nonzero payment, the contract's balance after the call must be zero, meaning all funds were forwarded to owner.
After any call to go(), the contract C's balance must be zero both before and after the call.
After any call to go(), the contract C's balance must be zero both before and after the call.
After any successful go call, the contract's balance must be zero both before and after the call.
After any call to go()—whether it succeeds or fails—the contract's balance must be zero both before and after the call.

After any call to go(), the contract's balance must become 0 because all remaining balance is transferred to the owner. The buggy version sends msg.value to a different address, reducing the balance available for the owner and leaving a non-zero balance in the contract.

After any call to go(), the contract's balance is always zero because all value is forwarded and the remainder is transferred to the owner, but the buggy version sends msg.value to 0x1 instead of the intended target, breaking the balance-zero invariant.
After any call to go(), the contract's balance is zero because the full balance is transferred to the owner; the bug sends msg.value to a different address, leaving a non-zero balance.

After go() succeeds, the owner's balance must increase by the contract's entire balance before the transfer, but the buggy version sends msg.value to 0x1, leaving less for the owner and breaking this invariant.
After a call to go(), if the contract's balance is greater than zero then the owner's balance must have increased.
A call to go() must not complete successfully unless the external low-level call to the fixed target also succeeds.
A call to go() must revert if the low-level call to the fixed target fails.
If go() does not revert, the external call must have succeeded, which implies the contract's balance must be zero after the transfer to owner.
go() reverts if and only if the balance of c is positive after the call.

The contract must always end with zero balance after go() because a failed external call returns false and the require makes it revert, preventing the owner transfer; the mutant skips the require, so when the call to the fixed target fails (returns false), the untransferred owner payment keeps the contract balance non-zero.

After any call to go(), the contract's balance must be zero because a failed external call reverts the whole transaction, whereas the mutant omits the require and leaves a non-zero balance when the external call fails.
After go() succeeds, the contract balance must be zero because the require causes revert on failed external call; the mutant omits require and leaves balance non-zero when the target call fails.

For any input where the target call returns false, the reference C's go() reverts leaving the contract balance unchanged, while the buggy version does not revert and leaves the contract balance non-zero.

Reference C always reverts when the target call fails, leaving the contract balance unchanged; the mutant skips the require, causing the contract to retain a non-zero balance equal to the sent value when the target call fails.
After any external call to go() with any msg.value, the reference contract always has zero balance, while the mutant retains msg.value.
After go() is called with any msg.value by any sender, the owner's balance increases by exactly that amount in the reference contract, while in the mutant it does not.

After calling go() with any msg.value, the contract's balance must be zero because the reference forwards all remaining ether to owner; the mutant retains the ether after the external call, leaving a non-zero contract balance for some input.

After any call to go() with any msg.value, address(this).balance of the reference contract is always zero because it forwards all remaining balance to owner, while the mutant retains the ether sent to target and thus has non-zero balance for some msg.value.
After any call to go(), the contract's balance is 0 for the reference contract, but the mutant leaves the sent Ether in the contract, so its balance can be non-zero.

After a call to go(), with any msg.value sent by an EOA, the owner's balance always increases by the full msg.value in the reference contract, but in the mutant the owner's balance increases by more than msg.value because the bug leaves msg.value inside the contract balance before transfer.

For any call to go() with msg.value > 0, the owner's balance always increases by exactly the msg.value sent, but the mutant increases the owner's balance by more than msg.value because it keeps the ether in the contract and transfers it along with any dust.

For any call to go() with msg.value > 0, the contract's balance after the call is 0, but the mutant leaves the sent Ether in the contract because the target.call value is zero, causing the balance to remain non-zero.

After any call to go() with any msg.value, the owner's balance never increases by more than msg.value in the reference, but the mutant can increase the owner's balance by more than msg.value because the sent Ether stays in the contract and gets transferred to the owner along with any pre-existing balance.
After any call to go(), the contract's entire ETH balance is always forwarded to the owner, whereas the buggy version may leave residual balance if msg.value > 1 ether.

After any call to go() with msg.value > 0, the owner's balance must increase by exactly the contract's entire balance (which is 1 ether if msg.value <= 1 ether), but the buggy version always transfers exactly 1 ether regardless of the contract's actual balance.

After go() is called, if any msg.value was sent, the owner's balance increases by exactly the amount sent (since the reference forwards the full balance which equals msg.value before the fixed external call succeeds and there are no other payers), but the buggy version may transfer a fixed 1 ether causing a mismatch when msg.value is not 1 ether.

After any call to go() with msg.value, the owner's balance must increase by the full contract balance left after the forward, which always equals msg.value, but the buggy version hardcodes a fixed 1 ether transfer.

After any call to go(), if the contract's balance after the external call is not exactly 1 ether, the owner's final balance reflects only a fixed 1 ether transfer in the mutant, while the reference transfers the full remaining balance.

After go() is called with Ether, the contract's balance is always transferred to the owner—the buggy version calls target (zero-address) which self-destructs, so the call succeeds but the Ether is permanently lost instead of being forwarded back to the owner, breaking the invariant that the final contract balance is zero.

After any call to go(), the owner's final balance equals its balance before the call plus the msg.value sent, because the contract always forwards its entire balance to the owner after a successful external call.

After go() is called, if the external call to target succeeds, the contract's balance must be zero because it transfers all remaining funds to the owner; the buggy version uses zero-address target where the call returns true but Ether is lost, leaving the contract with a nonzero balance.

After any call to go(), the contract's balance is zero, because the correct target always returns true and the contract then transfers its entire balance to the owner; the buggy target (zero address) also returns true but Ether sent to it is lost, so the contract retains a nonzero balance.
After any external call initiated by go() succeeds, the contract's ETH balance must become zero; the buggy version sends ETH to the zero address where it is lost, leaving a nonzero contract balance.

Regardless of whether the external call succeeds or fails, the owner should always receive the full balance of the contract after calling go(); the mutant fails to transfer any balance when the external call fails because the removed require allows execution to continue without reverting, leaving the contract with a zero balance but having already sent the call value.

After any call to go(), if the external call fails, the contract balance must be zero (owner received everything via transfer after revert); the mutant leaves the contract with the call value because the require is removed.

After go() is called, if the external call fails, the balance of c must be zero because the correct contract reverts; the buggy version leaves the contract balance non-zero when the external call fails.

For any call to go() with msg.value > 0, the contract C's balance must always be zero after the call (either all funds are forwarded on success, or the tx reverts on failure); the buggy version leaves a non-zero balance when the external call fails because the removed require skips the revert.

After a call to go() with a non-zero value, if the external low-level call fails, the contract C must have a zero balance (the transaction reverts); the mutant leaves the contract with a non-zero balance because the require is removed and execution continues.

After a call to go(), the contract's ETH balance must be zero because all funds are supposed to be transferred to the owner. The buggy version deletes the transfer, leaving the balance non-zero when msg.value > 0.

After any successful call to go() with msg.value > 0, the owner's balance must increase by exactly msg.value because all funds are forwarded; the buggy version leaves funds in the contract instead of transferring them to the owner.

After any call to go() with msg.value > 0, the contract's ETH balance must remain zero because all received funds are immediately forwarded to the hardcoded target; the buggy version omits the transfer to owner, so any excess remains in the contract.

After any call to go() with msg.value>0, the owner's ETH balance must equal their balance before the call plus msg.value; the buggy version omits the transfer so the owner's balance remains unchanged.

After any successful call to go() with msg.value > 0, the balance of contract C must equal msg.value minus the amount actually sent to the hardcoded target; the buggy version always leaves the full msg.value in the contract.
After any call to go, the owner's balance must equal the contract's entire balance; the buggy version only transfers 1 wei, leaving the remainder in the contract.
After a call to go, the contract's balance must be zero because the reference transfers the entire balance to the owner, while the buggy version leaves the remainder in the contract.

After any call to go(), the contract's balance must equal the owner's balance because the reference transfers the full contract balance to the owner, while the mutant leaves leftover ether in the contract.
After any call to go(), the contract's balance must be zero because the reference transfers the entire balance to the owner, while the buggy version leaves funds in the contract.

After any call to go(), the Ether held by the target address 0xC8A60C51967F4022BF9424C337e9c6F0bD220E1C must equal the Ether that was originally sent, because the reference transfers the full balance to the owner leaving no remainder to affect subsequent logic, while the mutant leaves leftover balance in the contract that can be force-sent to the target in later calls.

After a call to go with any value, the contract's ETH balance should remain 0 because all received value is forwarded; the buggy version keeps the ETH by sending 0 to the target, violating this invariant for any positive value.

After a call to `go` with some positive msg.value, the target contract 0xC8A60C51967F4022BF9424C337e9c6F0bD220E1C must receive at least the sent amount minus any gas; sending 0 instead of msg.value in the bug means the reference's `owner` receives strictly less ETH after `go` than the buggy contract's owner for some positive amounts, because the reference forwards all ETH to owner while the bug locks the received value in the contract.

For any call to go() with positive value, the reference contract’s owner balance strictly increases by that value (because ETH passes through to owner after a successful target call), while the buggy contract retains the ETH, so the owner balance does not increase.

For any call to go() with positive value, the target 0xC8A60C51967F4022BF9424C337e9c6F0bD220E1C receives exactly the sent msg.value in the reference, while the owner receives the remaining balance; in the buggy version the target receives 0, inflating the contract balance and changing the owner's eventual payout.

For any call to go() with positive value, the reference contract's balance after the call is 0 (since it forwards all received ETH to owner), while the buggy contract retains the sent value, leaving its balance equal to the sent amount.
After any successful call to go(), the contract's balance is zero because all remaining Ether is transferred to the owner.
After any successful call to go(), the contract's code size is non-zero because selfdestruct was not called; the buggy version calls selfdestruct, so the code size becomes zero.

After a successful call to go() with positive value, the contract's balance is zero; the buggy version selfdestructs, so the transfer sends Ether to the destroyed contract and the balance remains non-zero.

After any successful call to go(), the owner's balance increases by exactly msg.value, because the target call succeeds and the contract forwards its entire remaining balance to the owner; the mutant adds a selfdestruct, which destroys the contract and makes the subsequent transfer send Ether to an address with no code, leaving the owner's balance unchanged.

After a successful call to go() with any value, the contract's address(c).balance must be zero; the mutant inserts selfdestruct before the transfer, sending Ether to a destroyed contract and leaving the balance non-zero.

After any call to go(), the contract's ether balance is always zero, regardless of the outcome of the external call; the reference satisfies this, but the mutant may leave a non-zero balance if the external call fails.

After a successful call to go (no revert), the contract's own balance must be zero; the mutant violates this when the external call fails because it already transferred the balance to the owner before the call, leaving zero balance on failure but the property still holds—the actual violation is that in the mutant the owner receives address(this).balance *before* the external call instead of after, so on failure the owner keeps the transferred funds while the contract has zero balance, meaning the owner balance increases even when the external call reverts, breaking the invariant that owner only gets paid on success.

After a call to go() that does not revert, the contract's balance must be zero; the mutant transfers to owner before the external call, so if the external call fails and the caller's value is not forwarded, the owner still receives the contract's prior balance, violating the rule.
